80999.subject: The battle for Europe’s future
80999.body:
Editor's Digest 

Автор: Financial Times


Автор: Financial Times

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/battle-europes-future-financial-times-qnhic?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BMU3v3GX7RxO6gvMCKVPKeg%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=1DXubzFdsNOss1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mvc35w9v~nw-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mvc35w9v-nw
  
It has been a week of European exclusives for us at the FT. I travelled to Paris to meet Marine Le Pen, the frontrunner for the presidential election next year, and then on to Berlin for an interview with the conservative chancellor Friedrich Merz. The predicament of the two politicians — the first exceedingly confident, the second under growing pressure from a rising German far right — encapsulates the looming battle for Europe’s future. With a string of elections due across the continent, the far right could make significant gains in France, Poland, Italy and Spain and the mainstream will be fighting for relevance. In this excellent Big Read, our Europe editor explains exactly what’s at stake. In London, meanwhile, my colleagues sat down with a defiant Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who is furiously fighting back against pressure from Donald Trump. In another reflection of Europe’s trials, the US president continues to blame Ukraine and its leader, rather than Russia, for the war that Vladimir Putin launched. In the past week, Washington has agreed a cynical diesel deal with Moscow and restricted intelligence sharing with Kyiv. For Zelenskyy’s response, watch our interview here. My choices this week Thirty years ago, US television networks and venues wanted nothing to do with the Ultimate Fighting Championship. Now, its fights draw in politicians, celebrities and tycoons. This is the story of how Trump’s America fell in love with UFC. (Free to read) Yemen’s Houthis have made dramatic gains since their years-old conflict with Saudi Arabia reignited in July. Why is the Islamist group stepping up the fight? Eric Kutcher is the frontrunner in the race to become the next leader of McKinsey. But nothing is guaranteed in the consultancy’s conclave-style election system. Abdulrahman Alfozan was lauded as a rare Saudi national working for OpenAI. Then the ChatGPT maker found a bug wrapped in toilet paper at its headquarters. We uncover the fallout from Alfozan’s downfall. Aarav Dengla became a chess grandmaster at the age of just 16 earlier this year. In this refreshing column, Dengla explains how he used AI to get there — and how the technology can transform education for the better. (Free to read) Robert Armstrong suggests that instead of thinking of America’s economic recovery as K-shaped, we should imagine it as an E that’s leaning back a bit. Here’s why. Thanks

This week’s highlights: Billy Miller joins Schwab Network; Carlos Domingo joins NYSE Live; Securitize expands revenue potential; blockchain transforms finance; and tokenization unlocks collateral capital. Schwab Network Tokenizing Equities: SECZ COO on Adding Stocks to Blockchain, ARK Partnership Billy Miller explains how compliant, asset-backed tokenization can connect established securities with investors who prefer to transact onchain. WATCH NOW New York Stock Exchange Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo on Tokenized Stocks and the Future of Capital Markets In this NYSE Live interview, Carlos Domingo, CEO of Securitize, discusses the company's recent launch of Securitize Stocks, the growth of tokenized assets, and the broader evolution of blockchain-based financial infrastructure. WATCH NOW The Block StoneX Raises Securitize Price Target 50% as Tokenized Stock Platform Opens New Revenue Stream StoneX believes Securitize Stocks marks the company’s evolution from a tokenization vendor into a market operator with new transaction and servicing revenue. READ MORE Barron’s The Biggest Change to Stock Trading in Decades is Coming to Wall Street Blockchain-powered tokenization could transform Wall Street as profoundly as the shift from paper to electronic trading. READ MORE CNBC Tokenization Could Unleash Tens of Billions of Dollars in Trapped Capital, Nasdaq CEO Says Digitizing securities alongside money flows could make collateral more fluid across the global financial system, according to Nasdaq CEO Adena Friedman. 80931.subject: Team1 Japan: Institutions Chose Avalanche. Now It’s the Builders’ Turn.
80931.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.team1.blog/p/team1-japan-institutions-chose-avalanche

Team1 Japan is officially here.
Our mission is to build a Japanese builder community that matches the scale of Japan’s institutional adoption.
Here is what that means, and why Japan’s builder scene is unique.
The sequence is backwards, and that’s the opportunity
Japan’s institutions have already made their choice.
Progmat, the platform behind the majority of the country’s security token issuance, moved billions in tokenized real estate and corporate bonds onto a dedicated Avalanche L1. TIS, which processes more than half of Japan’s credit card volume, also launched its own L1. Some of the largest names in Japanese finance are now exploring tokenized government bonds using Avalanche infrastructure.
In most countries, this runs the other way. A community forms, developers experiment, projects ship, and eventually, sometimes years later, institutions notice and follow. Japan skipped the first half.
The chains themselves stay controlled, as Japanese financial regulation requires, but they no longer sit behind a wall. Gateways outward to wallets, to stablecoin settlement, and to applications written by people who were never invited into a private consortium are now being built. Japan’s financial system is no longer a closed circuit. It is growing an edge you can build against.
The demand is real, and the gateways to these platforms are underway.
That’s the gap Team1 Japan is here to close.
Want to keep up with the latest in the Avalanche ecosystem? Subscribe to the Team1 blog and get our updates in your inbox weekly.
What is Team1?
Team1 is a network of builders, developers, creators, event organizers, and community leaders working to grow the Avalanche ecosystem from the ground up. Since launching in 2024, it has grown to hundreds of members across more than 40 countries, with official chapters now live in the USA, Vietnam, India, Türkiye, Brasil, and across LatAm.
Team1 Japan is the newest of those chapters.
Our mandate is focused: connect Japan’s builders to Avalanche, and connect them to each other.
This is a formalization, not a beginning
Japan’s Avalanche community has been meeting for years.
Since April 2023, over 30 events have been held across Tokyo, Osaka, Nagoya, and Fukuoka with more than 1200 attendees between them. The anchor is Avalanche Gourmet Night, a series running for over two years that marks the beginning of the Avalanche community’s in-person presence
The programming has widened past meetups. Avalanche Academy study sessions have run four times since March, giving developers a recurring technical space rather than a social one. There have been collaborations with Uniswap Labs, zeroone, and Pudgy Penguins, and a workshop for teams who entered the JPYC stablecoin innovation challenge.
